signals.title: NOK/AUD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Jobs Shock Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows a 1.366% weekly performance spread between leader NOK (+0.672%, n=2) and laggard AUD (-0.694%, n=4), crossing the strong-theme threshold. Divergence is reinforced by domestic fundamentals: Australian employment contracted by 39,300 in September with unemployment rising to 4.7% (a 2.45σ shock), while the Norges Bank policy rate of 4.5% yields a +1.82% real rate against Australia's -0.70%. The bilateral carry deficit of 10bp (Norges Bank 4.5% vs RBA 4.6%) is fully offset by macroeconomic growth momentum and crude firmness at $94.1/bbl. AUD/USD trades at 0.6916, sitting firmly below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7010/0.7088/0.7044). Trade bias: Bearish AUD relative to European commodity FX; structural labor weakness invalidates further RBA tightening pricing. Catalyst: US Retail Sales and PPI at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp commodity rebound or RBA pushback on easing pricing invalidates the cross divergence.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Vol Complacency
signals.text: USD/JPY spot trades at 157.90, holding above its SMA20/50 cluster at 157.75/157.72 while testing below the SMA200 at 158.55. A 266bp OIS carry premium (SOFR 3.89% vs TONA 1.23%) keeps the base bid, but options markets show asymmetric hedging. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal sits at -1.70, reflecting pronounced demand for base downside protection even as 1M ATM IV of 7.6% runs 1.9 points below HV30 of 9.5%. That negative volatility risk premium indicates implied vol complacency relative to actual trading ranges. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY on tactical rallies; downside options hedging signals asymmetric vulnerability despite positive carry. Catalyst: BoJ policy decision on 30 Oct — hold expected. Risk: US Retail Sales surprise sharply higher at 12:30 UTC, triggering a nominal yield extension above the SMA200 at 158.55.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + CPI Repricing
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1211, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 structure (1.1312/1.1484/1.1592) following post-CPI dollar strength. CFTC leveraged funds positioning shows EUR net short at -84,775 contracts, sitting in the 4th percentile of its 52-week range (z = -1.64), marking an extended institutional short. Fed 4.00% (HIKING) vs ECB 2.65% (HIKING) creates a 135bp nominal policy rate spread in favor of USD, while the 20D US 5Y yield increase of +24bp (FRED, as of Oct 09) was real-yield-led (+30bp real vs -6bp breakeven). Spot is currently stretched vs model fair value (BEER z = -2.23σ at 1.1331). Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD; stretched short positioning limits follow-through selling into 1.1150 support. Catalyst: US Retail Sales and PPI at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US core inflation metrics accelerate further, driving 2Y yield spreads wider and initiating a fresh leg lower.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Short Extreme vs Policy Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD spot trades at 1.4203, holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 moving average cluster (1.4170/1.3990/1.3874). Retail sentiment data retail sentiment registers an extreme 93% short positioning, setting up a severe contrarian squeeze against the prevailing directional flow. Leveraged funds are heavily short CAD at -82,720 contracts (long% 21.2%), pointing in the opposite direction to retail positioning. The macro backdrop supports the spot advance, anchored by a 161bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.89% vs CORRA 2.28%) and a +175bp nominal policy rate differential (Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25%). Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by policy carry and potential retail capitulation. Catalyst: BoC Governor Macklem speech at 21:37 UTC. Risk: A clean break below the SMA20 anchor at 1.4170 triggered by unexpected crude strength.
